profile.headline: Sr. Software Engineer at DNA Software, Inc.

positions.title: Sr. Software Engineer
positions.description: Developing bioinformatics software, working in C++ on the back end analysis engines.

positions.title: Software Developer
positions.description: Supported development of C++ and C# applications for Siemens Medical Solutions as a contractor employed via Spherion.

positions.title: Senior Developer
positions.description: Developed high performance business informatics software, working in C++ on the back end analysis engine.

positions.title: Sr. Programmer/Analyst
positions.description:
Worked with chemists and biologists as a non-federal contractor developing software for scientific research, primarily in Fortran and also in C++.

Employing companies awarded the contract:
  1983/09 - 1993/09, Computer Sciences Corporation
  1993/10 - 1993/12, Atlantic Research Corporation
  1994/01 - 1995/09, Computer Sciences Corporation
  1995/10 - 1997/07, DynTel (a unit of DynCorp)

company.name: the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency research lab in Duluth, MN

positions.title: Applications Programmer
positions.description: Working on a U.S. EPA funded research project, designed and implemented software for an interactive chemical database.  Also designed graph theory algorithms to efficiently implement chemical structure analysis.  Work was primarily in Fortran, with some Pascal and assembly language.

publications.title: SMILES: A line notation and computerized interpreter for chemical structures.
publications.publisher: Report No. EPA/600/M-87/021. U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, Environmental Research Laboratory-Duluth, Duluth, MN 55804 · Jan 1, 1987

patents.title: Determining nucleic acid concentration by counting nucleic acid copies
patents.description: Provided herein is technology relating to quantifying the concentration of nucleic acids and particularly, but not exclusively, to methods for modeling data from a single quantitative amplification reaction, e.g., a PCR assay, to determine the initial concentration of a DNA target. In alternative embodiments, additional unknowns may be used, e.g., parameters for Bn, which is the concentration of probe at cycle n (and which changes in TAQMAN assays due to cleavage of the probe), EC for efficiency of probe cleavage, PDC for apparent probe dissociation constant, etc.
